title: Let `.extend()` replace or remove inherited abort signals
summary:
After this change, `.extend()` callers can drop signals inherited from a parent instance. `signal: replaceOption(newSignal)` replaces the parent signals, and `signal: undefined` removes them. Signal merging also now applies only to the root `signal` option. A nested key such as `json.signal` no longer gets pulled into the request signal.

In `deepMergeInternal`, a root `signal` key that is a replace marker or `undefined` empties the collected `signals` array. AbortSignal collection now requires `isRoot`. The readme and the `KyInstance.extend` JSDoc document the new behavior. Tests cover replace, removal, the nested JSON case, and an extra check that instance signals still combine with request signals.

changes.what: `deepMergeInternal` now unwraps `replaceOption` before signal handling. It clears `signals` when the root `signal` is a replace marker or `undefined`. It pushes AbortSignals only when `isRoot && key === 'signal'`. A typo in a comment is also fixed.
changes.why: Inherited signals can now be replaced or removed. Nested `signal` properties, for example inside `json`, now go through the normal merge path instead of being hoisted into the request signal.

changes.what: Extends the signal-merge test so an instance signal aborts a request that has its own signal. Adds three tests: replace via `replaceOption`, removal via `signal: undefined`, and nested `json.signal` handling.
changes.why: Covers the new clear and replace paths and the root-only scope.

changes.what: Adds a sentence on signal combining, `replaceOption(signal)`, and `signal: undefined` under `.extend()`.
Adds the same sentence to the `KyInstance` `.extend()` JSDoc.

risks.title: Per-request `signal: undefined` now drops instance signal
risks.reason: The clear applies to any root-level merge, not only `.extend()`. The existing test shows request options merge with instance signals through this path. A call like `api.get(url, {signal: opts.signal})` with an undefined `opts.signal` now empties `signals`. That silently discards the instance-level signal. The old code ignored a non-AbortSignal value here and kept the instance signal.

tests.description: Create `ky.create({signal: s})`, abort `s`, then call `api.get(url, {signal: undefined})`. Confirm whether the request still aborts. The old code aborts it; the new code does not.
Run `test/main.ts` and confirm the three new tests pass, plus the extended 'merges signals from instance and request options' test.
Chain `ky.create({signal: a}).extend({signal: replaceOption(b)}).extend({signal: c})`. Abort `a` and confirm no abort. Then abort `c` and confirm an abort.

Merge `json: {signal: someAbortSignal}` into an instance that has no prior `json`. Confirm the request body and the request signal match expectations, since nested signals now take the generic merge path.
Run the tests where `AbortSignal.any` is unavailable. Confirm that `replaceOption(signal)` still yields the replacement as `signals.at(-1)`.
